doc: A supply chain diagram whose values a YAML reader would type otherwise (FBL 0.5, sections 4.1.5 and 5.2): a group id written 01, a node id written 007 and another written "12", a name on, a year 2050. Every value reads as the text it was written with, so a node's group written 01 names the group 01 and a flow's end written 12 names the node "12"; the tool turns a number's text into its value and reports what will not read, which is why no number is written here. A legacy stage word is read as the stage it became (raw-material as source, retailer as outlet), a key the tool does not read is listed by the computed unknownKeys, an entry that is not a mapping is taken by the Unreadable rule, and an entry written as a flow mapping is a node whose members no key slot binds, read through the computed written attribute; it and the flow written with no id are reported as addressed by their place. Opening and saving without an edit writes the bytes that were read.

steps.doc: Opening and saving without an edit writes the bytes that were read, the plain 01, 007 and on and the quoted "12" included.
steps.expect:
supply-chain: 1
# What a supply chain diagram reads is what its author wrote.
groups:
  - id: 01
    name: Upstream
nodes:
  - id: 007
    type: raw-material
    name: on
    group: 01
  - id: "12"
    type: retailer
    name: 2050   # a year, not a number
    region: north
  - just text
  - {id: x, type: hub, name: X}
flows:
  - id: f1
    from: 007
    to: 12
    product: ore
  - from: 12
    to: 007
    product: scrap
